ICD-10-CM guideline navigator

The FY2025 Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting as a ranked hierarchy. Each of the 486 rules is scored on payment impact, disease severity, precision, specificity, strength, precedence, breadth and audit risk, then placed in tiers. Claims are grouped with the drgpy MS-DRG v43.1 grouper and priced at FY 2026 IPPS rates; each guideline finding is tested by regrouping the corrected codes, so the claim-level overpayment score counts only findings that would lower payment.

Find a rule

Tier 1 is the top 15% of rules by weighted score, Tier 2 the next 25%, Tier 3 the next 30%, Tier 4 the rest.

Scoring weights

Select a rule to see its plain-language meaning, score breakdown and full text.

Score claims for overpayment

.xlsx, .xls or .csv. One row per claim, or several rows per claim ID. Codes in a cell can be separated by commas, semicolons, pipes or spaces; dots are ignored. The first diagnosis is treated as principal. Each claim is grouped to an MS-DRG, priced, and gets one overpayment score (0–100), a title, its metrics, expected recovery and an explanation; there is no line-level output. Optional columns (sex, discharge status, length of stay, charges, paid amount, wage index) make grouping and pricing more exact.

Procedure codes (ICD-10-PCS)

The guidelines PDF covers ICD-10-CM only. Procedures are linked to the diagnosis rules they depend on.

Source: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2025 (NCHS/CMS, effective October 1, 2024), parsed from the PDF you supplied. Scores combine text analysis, hccpy CMS-HCC V28 coefficients for the codes each rule cites, and curated judgement for payment impact, audit risk and clinical acuity; each metric shows its source. Code titles come from the hcuppy FY2019 CCS files, so newer codes show as not found. MS-DRG grouping uses the drgpy package's CMS v43.1 definitions, ported to JavaScript and checked against the Python package; relative weights are from the CMS FY 2026 final rule Table 5 and rates from the FY 2026 IPPS final rule. Pricing follows the CMS IPPS Pricer steps but omits hospital-specific items you do not enter (IME, DSH, uncompensated care, new-technology add-ons, HRRP/HAC/VBP adjustments). Sustain rates are estimates, not fitted to audit outcomes; map an outcome column to check them. Scores prioritize review and are not coding determinations.
